answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol enforces cryptographic stake burning where verifying identity requires burning tokens at a superlinear cost scaling as O(N^2.5) for N identities. Every verified node broadcasts a beacon to anchor state, while ephemeral identities vanish like footprints on a shifting dune, unable to whisper illicit collusion across the network because replicating consensus weight demands exponential capital outlay.
